The user should expect to see similar power ratings between the two refrigerants, and a small variation in equipment size and costs. Input: Power Transmission Length Whereas this research effort solely focused on localized power from OTEC, the user is still given the ability to hypothetically assess an OTEC plant with power transmission. Power 24 OESI 2.0 M-1 T-1-P1.1 – Objective 3 Report April 2025 transmission is considered in this map as an added cost on a per-mile basis. In a case where the user wishes to explore supplying power to a different location than the oil and gas facility where the OTEC plant is located, the user may enter the distance (in miles) between the OTEC facility and the proposed power demand location. This distance will be used to reduce the available power output rating for electrical line losses and increase the capital costs for the additional equipment. Input: Financial Parameters Four additional parameters are used in the determination of the Real Levelized Cost of Electricity: the Interest Rate % (default of 0.07 or 7% is used), the Escalation Rate (Inflation) (default of 0.03 or 3% is used), the Tax Rate (default of 0.257 or 25.7% is used, based on NREL’s ATB assumptions (2024)), and the System Life (default of 30 years is used). The user is able to modify any or all of these financial parameters to calculate an LCOE based on their own assumed values for interest rate, escalation rate, and system life. These inputs can be made in the Real LCOE tab. 6.2 Model Outputs Based on the selected inputs, four main groups of output data are compiled by the model in addition to summarizing the ocean temperature data for the selected location: • OTEC Power rating data • Major equipment parameters • Process data • Real LCOE variables Output: OTEC Power Rating For the selected location, cold water intake pipe diameter, cold water intake depth, and refrigerant, the gross and net power are calculated for each month. The difference (which equals the calculated parasitic load and electrical losses) is shown for each month as a percentage of the gross power. The Annual Average Gross Power rating is calculated as the average of the twelve monthly average gross power values. Similarly, the Annual Average Net Power rating is calculated. In addition, the Winter Season Average Net Power is calculated by taking the average of the net power generated in January, February, and March. Lastly, the Peak Season Average Net Power is calculated as the average of the net power generated in July, August, and September when the surface water temperature is the warmest. 25 OESI 2.0 M-1 T-1-P1.1
